parole.significato: pertaining to, having relation with or qualities of
to repel; to push away (cause to move away)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese afastar, of obscure origin; maybe from Proto-Germanic *fastuz (“fixed, firm”), through Suevic [Term?] or Gothic.

parole.significato: to play, as in child's play or "playing around"
parole.testo: Probably from brinco (“merriment”) + -ar or less likely from Proto-Germanic *blinkaną (“to gleam, glitter, flash”).

From Old Galician-Portuguese galardon, gualardon, cognate with Spanish galardón; ultimately from Proto-Germanic *wiþrą (“against”) + *launą (“reward”), literally "back-payment". Compare Old French guerdon, Old High German widarlōn, Old English wiþerlēan.
From grampa, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *krampō (“cramp, clasp”), possibly via Old French crampe and/or Medieval Latin crampa; compare Galician grampa. See also cãibra.

parole.significato: distaff (part of a spinning wheel from which fibre is drawn to be spun)
parole.testo: Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *rukkô, although the intermediate language is uncertain. Possibly Gothic *𐍂𐌿𐌺𐌺𐌰 (*rukka), however, the vowel quality in Iberian Romance (/ɔ/ in Portuguese, /we/ in Spanish) points to a possible West Germanic loanword, or to the influence of Latin rota (“wheel”). Cognat
Maybe from Gothic *𐍄𐌰𐍀𐍀𐌰 (*tappa), Proto-Germanic *tappô, compare tapa, Italian tappo and English tap.
From Old Galician-Portuguese venda, from Proto-Germanic *binda; see also Old High German binta and German Binde.
